title: Stanford violated its AI policy by turning a Hispanic student into a fake Black woman in ad

reading.body:
This is a synthetic alteration of a documentary photograph rather than a generated one. A real student's likeness was replaced with another person's, and two other students were made to look thinner, and the result went onto campus banners as though it were the original picture. The failure sits in the production of public-facing advertising, at the point where an existing photograph of identifiable people is edited and then released with no indication that it was changed.

The check that would have caught it was a review of the finished banner against the source photograph and against the university's own policy before publication. Stanford's policy already prohibited using A.I. to produce or change images of Stanford people and events, and the university has said it is working with Residential and Dining Enterprises to provide more training and ensure proper review of all materials.

What is not established is intent, who carried out the edit, or whether anyone faced consequences, and the university's confirmation that the alteration and the lack of disclosure violated its policy is not a finding about why it happened.

reports.title: Stanford Used A.I. to Swap Black Student for Hispanic Student in a Photo
Stanford R&DE Uses AI to Race Swap Students for Advertising
University confirms use of AI-edited photo amid controversy
Stanford violated its AI policy by turning a Hispanic student into a fake Black woman in ad

summary:
In 2024, Stanford University's dining service posted a photo of Billy Ramirez, a Hispanic senior majoring in human biology, at a Lunar New Year party with two other students. Last week, when Stanford used the image on campus banners, Ramirez had been replaced by a Black woman, and the two other students were made to look thinner. Ramirez learned about the change from a friend and said it was upsetting, though he also saw a comedic element.

Stanford said on Tuesday that it had used artificial intelligence to alter the original image. The university said its policy strictly prohibits using A.I. to produce or change images of Stanford people, events, research, facilities, or achievements, and that both the alteration and the lack of disclosure violated that policy. Stanford added that it is working with Residential and Dining Enterprises to provide more training and ensure proper review of all materials.
title_en: Stanford violated its AI policy by turning a Hispanic student into a fake Black woman in ad
